newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher, approach 2,100 mark.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher, approach 2,100 mark.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Wednesday, helped by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to let interest rates stand for the moment, but the bourse's advance ran into resistance as the key indices neared the 2,100 mark.
"It looks like the Fed's move gives the bourse a month and a half of breathing space," until after the U.S. presidential election, a trader said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 12.82 points, or 0.62 percent, at 2,094.32 at 0830 GMT after easing from an early high of 2,098.13. The CAC-40 futures contract was up nine points at 2,095 after retreating from a resistance level at 2,098.
Volume was 540 million francs in the first half hour.

Traders said the bourse was performing well, with demand emerging at every dip, but they said investors were carefully watching Wall Street's reactions, the dollar's level and news about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
A stream of first-half corporate results triggered activity in individual shares.
Shares in insurer Axa jumped 2.6 percent at 293.40 francs after the group reported a bigger-than-expected jump in net attributable profit to 1.98 billion francs for the first half.
